newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee convertibility steps possible in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: India rupee convertibility steps possible in 97/98.

text.p: India can take steps this fiscal year towards making the rupee convertible on capital account if inflation remains stable and the fiscal deficit is cut, the central bank chief was quoted on Thursday as saying.

"It is feasible to take some measures towards capital account convertibility if the inflation rate continues to hover around the present six percent and the fiscal deficit is restricted to around 4.5 percent during the year," United News of India quoted Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor C. Rangarajan as saying in an interview.
A committee appointed by the RBI earlier this month submitted its recommendations for a convertible rupee by the turn of the century.
The panel listed preconditions needed before India fulfils its plans to make the rupee fully convertible.

Those included an average inflation rate of three to five percent for the three-year period until 2000, and a reduction in the fiscal deficit to gross domestic domestic (GDP) ratio to 3.5 percent by 1999/2000 (April-March) financial year.
India's year-on-year inflation rate measured by the wholesale price index fell to 5.93 percent in the week ended May 31 from 6.00 percent in the previous week, the Industry Ministry said on Sunday.
The fiscal deficit as a share of the gross domestic product (GDP) was estimated at 5.0 percent in 1996/97.
The government has set the fiscal deficit target at 4.5 percent of GDP for 1997/98, and aims to cut the deficit to below 4.0 percent in 1998/99.

Rangarajan told the news agency: "We are looking into the interactive process between the liberalisation of capital transaction and the crucial preconditions so that certain transactions related to capital account can be identified for relaxation under the present economic environment."
The rupee was made convertible on the current account of the balance of payments in August 1994.
